newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds see thin interest pre-supply.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds see thin interest pre-supply.

text.p: *Australian bonds were limited to a relatively narrow trading range ahead of Tuesday's A$900 million two-tranche Treasury bond tender.
*U.S. Treasuries face quarterly refunding this week.
Australian bonds were limited to a relatively narrow trading range ahead of Tuesday's A$900 million two-tranche Treasury bond tender with the longer of the two expected to see keen interest.
The Treasury will be offering A$300 million of January 2001 and A$600 million of November 2006 stocks.
"I think the market will happily take up the 2006 bonds. The stock is pretty tight, particularly in the repo market," one trader said.
Final bids are due in on Tuesday at 12.45 (0145 GMT) and the result will be announced at 2.00 p.m. (0300 GMT).

A dip in U.S. Treasury bond prices in early Tokyo trading had weighed on the domestic market after the U.S. dollar fell sharply after this weekend's G7 meeting, which said it believed the major misalignments in exchange markets had been corrected.
However, both U.S. markets mostly recovered during the course of the day.
U.S. Treasuries face the quarterly refunding auctions this week, which total US$39.75 billion and kick-off on Tuesday with US$17.75 billion of three-year notes.
Reaction to the sales are expected to heavily influence the direction of the local market this week.

Meanwhile, the market got an insight into this Thursday's Australian labour force report with the release of the ANZ jobs series for January, which rose 3.3 percent after a revised 2.3 percent fall in December.

ANZ chief economist Saul Eslake said while the two-year decline in demand for labour appears to be coming to an end, he warned that the job ads data needed to be treated with caution given that summer is usually a volatile period.
January employment is seen rising 10,000 after December's 4,500 increase, while unemployment is forecast unchanged at 8.6 percent, according to a Reuters survey of economists.

Local bonds dragged their heels against U.S. and Canadian debt throughout the day ahead of Tuesday's tender. However, New Zealand bonds also under-performed following an initial fall in the N.Z. dollar. The local yield curve remained around last week's flatter level.
